label: rem:hopf-link-non-magic
title: Hopf link as the canonical non-magic knot operator (lowest cohomological degree)
html:
Remark. Hopf link as the canonical non-magic knot operator (lowest cohomological degree)

Hopf link as the simplest knot operator. The Hopf link T_{2,2} is the simplest non-trivial 2-component link in the framework's knot-operator basis:

  • Crossing number 2 (minimum for any non-trivial link).
  • Hyperbolic volume 0 (Seifert-fibered, not hyperbolic).
  • Complement S^3 \setminus \mathrm{Hopf} \simeq T^2 — cohomology rank \leq 2 in every degree.
  • Multivariable Alexander polynomial \Delta(t_1, t_2) = 1 (the standard convention for 2-component links is the multivariable form; the single-variable \Delta(t) = 0 for the Hopf link in the literature should not be confused with this). In the QOU framework's reading the Hopf link is the by definition-non-trivial link — its Alexander structure carries no signed information, which is the link-theoretic fact behind its E^{0, *}-only cohomological location.
  • Fundamental group: \mathbb{Z} \oplus \mathbb{Z} — abelian.

Cohomological location in the framework. The Hopf link lives entirely in the E_\infty^{0, *} slot of the brane-tower spectral sequence (conj:mass-endomorphism) — the descended Markov-trace piece. It contributes only the E^{0, *} component of the SDP optimum (prop:knot-operator-selection).

Non-magic shells use the Hopf link. At non-magic n at substrate q_0, the SDP optimum T^*(n, q_0) is Hopf-decomposable, expressible as a tensor product of Hopf links and trivial ribbons. It lives entirely in E_\infty^{0, *} (the descended Markov-trace piece per conj:mass-endomorphism).

Magic shells require higher-cohomology operators. At magic n, the SDP optimum requires non-trivial contribution from E_\infty^{p, q \geq 1} — operators NOT Hopf-decomposable. By prop:torus-knot-shell-binding, the active operator at each magic n is one of the six Bring-embeddable torus knots \{T_{2,3}, T_{2,5}, T_{2,7}, T_{2,9}, T_{3,4}, T_{3,5}\}, none of which is Hopf-decomposable.

Operational reading of the magic predicate. Selection of the active knot operator at strand count n is a topological-class decision:

n class Active knot operator Cohomological grading
non-magic Hopf-decomposable (e.g. T_{2,2}^{\otimes k}) E_\infty^{0, *}
magic non-Hopf Bring torus knot (T_{p, q} with q \geq 3, p \in \{2, 3\}) E_\infty^{p \geq 1, q \geq 1}

This matches the empirical mass-decomposition observation (conj:mass-endomorphism) that descended \mathrm{tr}_M contributes \lesssim 0.5\% of magic-shell binding; the rest is brane-tower (= higher-cohomological) contribution.
